variable {R S T : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] [CommRing T]

/-- A ring hom `R →+* S` is quasi-finite if `S` is a quasi-finite `R`-algebra. -/
@[algebraize RingHom.QuasiFinite.toAlgebra]
def QuasiFinite {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S) : Prop :=
  @Algebra.QuasiFinite R S _ _ f.toAlgebra

/-- Helper lemma for the `algebraize` tactic -/
lemma QuasiFinite.toAlgebra {f : R →+* S} (hf : QuasiFinite f) :
    @Algebra.QuasiFinite R S _ _ f.toAlgebra := hf

variable {R S : Type*} [CommRing R] [CommRing S] (f : R →+* S)

lemma quasiFinite_algebraMap [Algebra R S] :
    (algebraMap R S).QuasiFinite ↔ Algebra.QuasiFinite R S := by
  rw [RingHom.QuasiFinite, toAlgebra_algebraMap]
=== Algebra.QuasiFinite ===
/--
We say that an `R`-algebra `S` is quasi-finite
if `κ(p) ⊗[R] S` is finite-dimensional over `κ(p)` for all primes `p` of `R`.

This is slightly different from the
[stacks projects definition](https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/00PL),
which requires `S` to be of finite type over `R`.

Also see `Algebra.QuasiFinite.iff_finite_comap_preimage_singleton` that
this is equivalent to having finite fibers for finite-type algebras.
-/
@[mk_iff, stacks 00PL]
class QuasiFinite : Prop where
  finite_fiber (P : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime] :
    Module.Finite P.ResidueField (P.Fiber S) := by infer_instance

attribute [stacks 00PM] quasiFinite_iff

namespace QuasiFinite

attribute [instance] finite_fiber

instance [QuasiFinite R S] (P : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime] : IsArtinianRing (P.Fiber S) :=
  .of_finite P.ResidueField _

lemma finite_comap_preimage_singleton [QuasiFinite R S] (P : PrimeSpectrum R) :
    (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' {P}).Finite :=
  (PrimeSpectrum.preimageEquivFiber R S P).finite_iff.mpr finite_of_compact_of_discrete

lemma finite_primesOver [QuasiFinite R S] (I : Ideal R) : (I.primesOver S).Finite := by
  by_cases h : I.IsPrime
  · refine ((finite_comap_preimage_singleton ⟨I, h⟩).image PrimeSpectrum.asIdeal).subset ?_
    exact fun J hJ ↦ ⟨⟨_, hJ.1⟩, PrimeSpectrum.ext hJ.2.1.symm, rfl⟩
  · convert! Set.finite_empty
    by_contra!
    obtain ⟨J, h₁, ⟨rfl⟩⟩ := this
    exact h inferInstance

lemma finite_comap_preimage [QuasiFinite R S] {s : Set (PrimeSpectrum R)} (hs : s.Finite) :
    (PrimeSpectrum.comap (algebraMap R S) ⁻¹' s).Finite :=
  hs.preimage' fun _ _ ↦ finite_comap_preimage_singleton _

## Verdict: CHURNING, with one real result underneath

The reduction lemmas of §2–§3 are genuine and correct. What was published on top of them — the strength ordering, the producer's meaning, and the three-row multiplier — does not survive checking. Four commits in 22 minutes, each announcing a new "reduction", where the second, third and fourth add names to steps already reachable, and the fourth's headline ("nothing between them is unbuilt") is false.

Nothing is sorried, nothing is axiomatic (`#print axioms` clean on all 7 I sampled), the file builds, HEAD matches disk, no scratch file reached the ledger. The failure mode is over-pricing, not fabrication.

### Findings, most severe first

**1. CONFIRMED — "nothing between the fibrewise antecedent and finiteness is unbuilt" is false; the support/fibre bridge does not exist.** (`isFinite_support_of_fibers` docstring, commit `e38b77368d`.) The antecedent quantifies over `Hom.fiber (schematicSupportι x.F ≫ pullback.snd π T.hom) t` — the fibre of the support. The `DivDegree.lean` fibre SES the docstring points the producer at (`fiberCokernelIso`, etc.) is about `Hom.fiberModule (pullback.snd π T.hom) t x.F`, whose support is `schematicSupport (fiberModule …)` — the support of the fibre. `rfl` fails between the two carriers. And there is no lemma relating them: `QuotSupportBaseChange.lean:498` proves only `annihilator F ≤ (annihilator (g'^* F)).map g'`, the direction that yields properness of the larger support. The reverse inclusion is nowhere in the project. So the recommended target carries an unnamed second obligation, and it is exactly the one the cited names cannot supply. This is the answer to your question 5: the remaining obligation is *not* only "a nonempty effective Cartier divisor on a relative curve has finite fibres".

**2. CONFIRMED — the "strictly weaker" fibrewise form is interderivable with the point-set form at the site you recommend it for.** Probed both directions at a `DivFamily`, where `properSupport` is a field: fibrewise ⇒ point-set (compose your own `of_fibers` with your own `iff`), and point-set ⇒ fibrewise (`of_finite_preimage_singleton`, then `IsProper` from the field, then `inferInstance` per fibre). Both close. The ordering is true for an arbitrary module and empty at a family — so commit `39d8a923e9`, whose whole subject is "FIBREWISE, needing no proper support", bought a spelling at the only site a producer will stand.

**3. CONFIRMED — the producer at `DivFamily.zero` buys less than claimed, and was already one `inferInstance` away.** Two measurements: (a) at `DivFamily.zero` the *consequent* is free with no binder — `CoherentSheafFlat (𝟙 T.left) (q_* O_D)` closes by `Modules.coherentSheafFlat_of_isZero (Functor.map_isZero _ (isZero_zero _))`, and `isFinitePresentation_pushforward` likewise by `isFinitePresentation_of_isZero`. So "their conclusions become facts about an actual family" delivers nothing that was not already one line from `DivFamilyZero.lean`. (b) With only the pre-existing `isEmpty_schematicSupport_of_isZero` in scope, plain `infer_instance` closes both `LocallyQuasiFinite` and `IsFinite` of the support map at zero. The file's own I-1494 caveat is honest about geometry-vs-satisfiability, but stops short of this.

**4. CONFIRMED — the "three rows" value claim holds for one row.** D4′ (campaign `:324`) consumes D3′; it never binds `LocallyQuasiFinite`, so counting it double-counts the same discharge. `HasLocallyConstantDivDeg` (`DivDegree.lean:629`) demands `IsLocallyConstant x.fiberDeg` — local constancy of a rank function — and its own docstring names *two* inputs: "the finiteness/rank half of the B3 rigid-pushforward engine **plus** relative-dimension-1 quasi-finiteness". This file supplies at most one.

**5. CONFIRMED — the def-vs-class caveat is real but the diagnosis is wrong, in the direction that inflates the work.** `haveI := hps; infer_instance` does fail (reproduced, both goals); `haveI : IsProper _ := hps` does fix it. But `locallyOfFiniteType_schematicSupportι_comp` is `hps.toLocallyOfFiniteType` — a structure-parent projection, probed and closing — and the quasi-compact one is one hop via `hps.toUniversallyClosed`. "Both follow by synthesis" and "reads as *mathlib lacks IsProper ⟹ LocallyOfFiniteType*, which is false" describe a field access.

**6. CONFIRMED — the `schematicSupportι` docstring's sub-claim is stated backwards.** It says `infer_instance` fails after `unfold` "because unfolding replaces the reducible definition by the `annihilator`-projection form that the instance is not indexed on". With `pp.explicit`: `unfold` rewrites only the *source scheme* (`schematicSupport X F` → `IdealSheafData.subscheme`); the morphism is `IdealSheafData.subschemeι` either way, and the goal stated *directly* at the annihilator spelling also fails `infer_instance`. The `inferInstanceAs` is load-bearing (your instinct was right — this is not a duplicate of an available instance; `infer_instance` fails at both spellings), but the published explanation sends the next reader hunting a reducibility bug.

**7. CONFIRMED — one cited name does not resolve as written.** `isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel` is `Scheme.DivFamily.isLocallyTrivial_fiber_kernel` (`DivDegree.lean:275`); `#check` at `Scheme.Modules.…` from inside the import closure gives `unknownIdentifier`. No declaration is `P → P` or a restatement of a tree/mathlib lemma under another name. `horizon search` finds no prior art for the composite forms; the `schematicSupportι` theorem is not noise (both spellings fail `infer_instance`). §2–§3 as *statements about an arbitrary module with proper support* are correct, new, and useful: the equivalence `binder ↔ finite fibres` is a real repricing of D3′'s hypothesis, and it is the one thing here that would have cost the next lane time to rediscover.
